title: Implementation of pediatric advance care planning in Bavaria
summary: Advance Care Planning refers to a professionally facilitated communication process in which patients, family members, and healthcare professionals are supported in jointly reaching decisions regarding desired future medical treatment. To date, Germany lacks a nationwide, structured Advance Care Planning program for children and adolescents. The aim of this project is to implement a structured Advance Care Planning concept for children and adolescents in palliative care, their legal guardians, and the professionals involved, in Bavaria. Questionnaires, focus groups, expert interviews, and a constellation analysis will be used to identify the facilitating and hindering factors for successful implementation. Together with patients, parents, and the professionals involved, strategies for optimizing the implementation of decisions made through Advance Care Planning in clinical practice will be developed and piloted.
conditions: The lack of a widely available, structured Advance Care Planning offer for children and adolescents in Germany.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
– Parents or legal guardians of children/adolescents cared for by one of the eight participating SAPV-KJ teams in Bavaria who undergo a pediatric Advance Care Planning (pACP) process.
– Parents or guardians acting as legal representatives for individuals over the age of 18 who are receiving care from one of the six SAPV-KJ teams in Bavaria participating in the study and are undergoing a pediatric advance care planning (pACP) process.
– Parents or legal guardians for whom the documents created during the pACP process have already been implemented.
– Professionals involved in conducting pACP processes.
– Network partners involved in implementing decisions made during the pACP process, and network partners who have experienced the implementation of pACP process decisions.
Exclusion criteria:
For parents or legal guardians:
– Insufficient German language proficiency that precludes a complete understanding of the study information and the pACP process, as well as informed consent.
– Significant psychological burden, where, in the assessment of the respective SAPV-KJ team, study participation is not reasonably feasible at the given time.

For professionals and network partners:
– Lack of experience with, or lack of involvement in, pACP processes.
